To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intracerebro-ventricular delivery of AAV9 in adult rats and pigs results in high levels of transduction of the brain with a dose-response relationship.

intracerebroven-tricular delivery of self-complimentary adeno-associated virus to the adult rat central nervous system is safe, and that the level of transduction can be increased by increasing the dose.

self-complementary AAD9 can be used to transduce the adult rat brain at doses as low as 1.25 × 1011 vector genomes, and the transduction efficiency is dose-dependent, with the highest efficiency observed at a dose of 2.5 × 1012 vector genomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of AAV9-based gene therapy for the central and peripheral nervous systems.
the delivery of gene-based therapies to the central nervous system using self-complementary AIV9 delivered i.c.v.
the development of AAV9 as a gene delivery vector for use in the central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
i.c.v.-injected self-complementary AAAV9 is a promising candidate for gene therapy for neurological disorders in the adult brain.
self-complementary AAA9 is a strong candidate for gene therapy of numerous central nervous system diseases.
self-complementary A.A.V.-9 is a safe vector and that it is effective at delivering genes to the central nervous system of the adult rat when administered i.c.v.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dose–response curve for self-complementary AAY9 in the rat is similar to that of the neonatal mouse.

the intracerebro-ventricular delivery of a single injection of self-complementary serotype 9 adeno-associated virus to adult rats and pigs results in widespread transduction throughout the brain and cerebrospinal fluid.

i.c.v. delivery of self-complimentary adeno-associated virus 9 to the brain and spinal cords of neonatal and adult mice and rats is a safe and efficient way to achieve widespread transduction of the central nervous system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
i.c.v. delivery of self-complimentary, AAV9 to the adult brain results in widespread transduction of neurons and astrocytosis is not observed at the doses tested.
i.c.v. delivery of self-complimentary adeno-associated viral vectors is a promising approach for gene delivery in the brain.
i.c.v. delivery of self-complimentary adeno-associated viral serotype 9 is an efficient means of delivering transgenes to the adult rat central nervous system.
